territorial_scope.description: Applies to Connecticut state agencies, the Judicial Department and state contracting agencies, and through contract terms to businesses contracting with them.

evidence.quote: the Office of Policy and Management shall develop and establish policies and procedures concerning the development, procurement, implementation, utilization and ongoing assessment of systems that employ artificial intelligence and are in use by state agencies

summary.short: Requires Connecticut state agencies and the Judicial Department to inventory their AI systems and to assess them for unlawful discrimination or disparate impact before implementation, and requires state contracts with businesses to include privacy-act compliance clauses. Sections 1-3 take effect July 1, 2023.
summary.long: Substitute Senate Bill 1103 (approved June 7, 2023) governs artificial intelligence use in Connecticut state government. Section 1 requires the Department of Administrative Services to inventory state agencies' AI systems annually, first by December 31, 2023, publish the inventory, and assess the systems from February 1, 2024 for unlawful discrimination or disparate impact. Section 2 requires the Office of Policy and Management to set procurement, implementation and assessment policies by February 1, 2024, and bars state agencies from implementing AI systems without a prior impact assessment or where the agency head determines discrimination or disparate impact would result. Section 3 imposes parallel duties on the Judicial Department. Section 4, from October 1, 2023, requires state contracts with businesses to require compliance with sections 42-515 to 42-525 of the general statutes. Section 5, effective on passage, creates a working group to make recommendations on AI use in state government and private-sector regulation, reporting by February 1, 2024. The sections state no penalties.

notes: Relations list only references stated in this text. No enabling act, amendment, repeal or implementation is stated. Several terms (State agency, business, contract) and the Sec. 4 contract duty depend on general statutes not reproduced here, so the text cannot be read standalone. The AI definition recurs in Secs. 1, 2, 3 and 5 with different lettering but the same substance. Sec. 1 binds the Department of Administrative Services, Sec. 2 the Office of Policy and Management, Sec. 3 the Judicial Department. Effective dates differ by section: July 1, 2023 (Secs. 1-3), October 1, 2023 (Sec. 4), from passage (Sec. 5).

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff that changes the legal treatment of a person, entity or system was found. Statutory dates (December 31, 2023; February 1, 2024; October 1, 2023), the 30-day and 60-day appointment and meeting periods, and the 50 per cent working-group quorum are procedural time limits or internal governance rules, so they are not coded as thresholds. The Act's obligations apply to state agencies and the Judicial Department without size, revenue or user cutoffs.
